candidates.statement: Since the first cusp is an unknot (in $S^3$), it follows from the classification of lens spaces, that all Dehn fillings of $W$ or $P$ yielding a knot in $L(p,q)$ must have filling coefficients obtained from the following operations \begin{align} (p,q) &\mapsto (p,q+np), & \forall n \in \mathbb{Z} \label{lenspace_1}\\ (p,q) &\mapsto (p,q^*), & q^*q \equiv 1 \mod p \label{lenspace_2}\\ (p,q) &\mapsto (-p,q), (p,-q). \label{lenspace_3} \end{align} The volume functions ($\vol_W-\Delta \vol_W(p,q)$, for $\vol_W(p,q)$ from Equation \ref{eq:DvolP} and the correspondingly for $P$) derived by Hodgson and Masai in \cite{Hodgson_Masai} exclude all but finitely many fillings slopes satisfying \Cref{lenspace_1,lenspace_2,lenspace_3} from being volume minimising.

candidates.statement: Inserting this into the first terms of \Cref{eq:DvolW,eq:DvolP}, we can see that---for $p$ sufficiently large---the minimiser must be obtained by filling slope $(p, -1)$ on $W$ (setting $p\geq 0$ without loss): For $(p,\pm 1)$, the function $\Delta \vol_P (p,q)$ converges to $\frac{\pi^2}{2p^2}$ plus lower order terms, while $\Delta \vol_W (p,q)$ converges to $\frac{2\pi^2}{p^2}$ plus lower order terms; and we have $\Delta \vol_W (p,-1) = \frac{2\pi^2}{p^2 -4p + 1}$ while $\Delta \vol_W (p,1) = \frac{2\pi^2}{p^2 +4p + 1}$.

candidates.statement: Since we can efficiently compute ∆volW (p, q) and ∆volP (p, q) up to error terms in p (and q), this distance must be considered with respect to the magnitude of p (and q).

We devise such a procedure by determining how many terms of the Taylor series expansion of ∆volW and ∆volP we must consider, in order to certify that they have distinct function values at pi qi , aj bj ∈Q.
